resources.string: Connect another device through your phone
First, on the phone running SplateVPN
Choose a working server in SplateVPN and connect. For testing, the All traffic route is convenient.
Settings → Share VPN over LAN. Choose an interface and wait for the VPN to reconnect. On the other device, enable proxy authentication: username splate and the password shown in sharing settings.
Enable the phone\'s hotspot and connect the other device over Wi-Fi. A computer supporting Android USB tethering can use USB instead. A shared LAN also works if client isolation is disabled.
For Android and iPhone/iPad, connect to the phone\'s hotspot over Wi-Fi. Configure the proxy for that network.
For a Mac, use Wi-Fi or a shared LAN. Android USB tethering support depends on the phone and driver; Wi-Fi is the main option.

This shares a proxy connection. It works in browsers and apps that honor the system proxy or provide their own proxy settings. Games, calls and other apps may bypass it; the device\'s entire traffic does not automatically enter the VPN.
VPN is disconnected. Connect it on the home screen.
Sharing is not running yet. Enable it and wait for the VPN to reconnect.
Enable the hotspot or USB tethering. You can read the guide now; connection parameters become copyable after an address is detected. The address may change next time.
Choose the network used by the other device. Wi-Fi and USB addresses can differ.
This is an illustration; labels and appearance vary by OS version.
Enter only the IP, without http:// or a port. Authenticate with splate and the password from sharing settings. HTTP and HTTPS use the HTTP port; SOCKS5 has its own port.
For bash / zsh and programs honoring these variables. Applies only to this terminal and programs launched from it; GUI apps and sudo may not use them.
Use PowerShell, not CMD. Changes the current user\'s proxy for apps honoring Windows settings. Replaces the previously configured proxy address.
Test the HTTP proxy with curl
The response should contain example.com HTML. This tests a proxy connection, not the route of the entire device.
Open a website on the other device
Use a browser honoring the system proxy. Try a site that should open through the VPN. Traffic follows the route selected in SplateVPN.
If an app does not work
It may ignore the system proxy. If the app has proxy settings, choose SOCKS5 and enter the phone address and SOCKS5 port. Without such settings, this method may not work for that app.
The IP may change after restarting the hotspot. Use the current address from the Device step. HTTP and HTTPS use the HTTP port, not the SOCKS5 port.
Both devices must be able to reach each other on the same network. Guest Wi-Fi, client isolation, phone sleep or another VPN on the receiving device can interfere.
VPN and sharing must be enabled. If the site fails on the phone, fix VPN first. Use the proxy password and share with trusted devices.
If you imported a full JSON profile
Local proxy ports are managed by the app. Use the HTTP/SOCKS5 addresses from this guide.
Turn the proxy off when finished
Settings → Wi-Fi / Internet → the hotspot network → its settings or edit icon.
Open Modify network or Advanced options → Proxy → Manual. Labels vary on Samsung, Xiaomi and other devices.
Fill in the fields and save
Proxy hostname is the SplateVPN phone\'s IP; port is the HTTP port below. Leave the network\'s IP settings on DHCP / automatic.
Settings → Wi-Fi → ⓘ next to the phone\'s hotspot network.
Server is the phone IP; port is the HTTP port below. Enable authentication with splate and the sharing password, then save.
Manual proxy setup → Set up / Use a proxy server → On.
Enter the IP and HTTP port
Fill in the illustrated fields below and save. These are the current user\'s proxy settings, not a Windows VPN connection.
System Settings → Network → Wi-Fi or Ethernet → Details → Proxies.
Enable Web proxy (HTTP) and Secure web proxy (HTTPS). Enter the same IP and HTTP port for both.
Enable proxy authentication with splate and the sharing password. Click OK / Done, then Apply. SOCKS need not be enabled at the same time.
Ubuntu / GNOME: Settings → Network → Network Proxy. Choose Manual.
Enter the same phone IP and HTTP port in both rows. Save; some apps need to be restarted.
KDE Plasma: search for Proxy in System Settings → choose manual configuration.
Enter the phone IP and HTTP port for HTTP and HTTPS, then Apply. Apps may have their own proxy settings.
Copy and run the commands below in your terminal. Then launch the commands you need from that same terminal.
Open the app\'s Proxy section, often found under network or data settings.
Enter the phone IP and SOCKS5 port below. Username is splate; use the sharing password. For HTTP-only apps, use the HTTP port.
In this Wi-Fi network\'s settings, set Proxy → None and save.
Settings → Wi-Fi → ⓘ → Configure Proxy → Off → Save.
Settings → Network & internet → Proxy → Use a proxy server → Off.
Network → your connection → Details → Proxies: turn HTTP and HTTPS off and save.
Run the unset command below or close this terminal.
Set Network Proxy back to None / Disabled.
Turn the proxy off in the app\'s own settings.
Otherwise those apps may lose internet access after the phone disconnects.

While connected, checks public pages every 5 minutes using the selected SmartDNS mode. Repeated failures trigger a verified replacement and a brief VPN reconnect. CAPTCHA and sign-in are not failures.
DNS queries and the SmartDNS proxy connection use the selected VPN server. Auto-selection tests this same route. Service access also depends on the SmartDNS exit region and account settings.
Tests providers in the selected mode and applies a confirmed option. Direct mode also tests TLS fragmentation. May take a few minutes.
Checks DNS, HTTPS and public Gemini, ChatGPT and Claude pages. Finalists also load Gemini with JavaScript. Account sign-in and functionality are not checked.
The automatic check could not confirm Gemini. It may still work in your browser: sign-in and WebView restrictions can prevent verification. Settings unchanged. Details below.
Could not complete the check. Settings unchanged.
DNS returned no valid public IPv4
JavaScript page loaded; account not checked
JavaScript: sign-in, CAPTCHA or page error
browser check requires Android 9+ and an up-to-date Android System WebView
Checks use the current connection and routing rules. Website availability does not guarantee login, streaming or calls.
DNS and server port use the physical network; HTTPS uses VPN. An open port does not confirm valid credentials.

AND requires all filled fields to match; OR requires any one. Lines within a field are alternatives. The first matching rule applies.
Match apps, domains, IPs, ports and protocols. App conditions need Android 10+ and inclusion in VPN on the Apps screen.
Rules are saved but do not apply in Tor mode.
Custom exceptions and essential DNS rules run first. Combined rules run before subscription and region rules.
Saved rules are invalid. The VPN will not use an unvalidated set.
Matching traffic goes directly, outside the VPN server.
One package ID per line, case-sensitive. Uninstalled apps stay in the rule. Shared-UID apps are unsupported.
App conditions require Android 10 or later.
One domain per line. Matches the domain and its subdomains. A leading dot is optional.
Multiple lines within a field mean OR. Empty fields are ignored.
Enable domain detection for these rules
Manually entered packages stay selected even when absent from this list.
With your consent, reports contain only the error type, code locations and app version. IP addresses, device data, exception messages, logs, subscriptions and settings are excluded.
No automatic sending: there is no report receiver. Up to five reports stay on this device. Disabling collection deletes them.
Export opens the system menu. You choose the recipient.
Paste a link to a JSON backup file. The client downloads it and shows its contents before restoring. No folder selection is needed.
Password, if the backup is encrypted
Google Drive, Yandex Disk, Dropbox and direct HTTPS links. The file must be accessible without signing into a cloud account. Plain backups need no password.
Folder selection was removed from cloud backup. Existing files and the encryption password were kept. Restore using a backup link, or configure WebDAV for background backups.
Encrypted backups every 6 or 24 hours. Restore after review and confirmation. The last 10 snapshots from this device are kept separately.
Uses WebDAV saved under transfer settings. A conflicting shared copy is kept: download and review it before syncing again.
Background backup stores the password encrypted with Android Keystore on this device only. Keep it separately: another device needs it to restore.
Passwords must match and contain at least 8 characters
Review the receiving device and confirm sending.
Connect your phone and TV to the same Wi-Fi or Ethernet network. Servers, subscriptions, Tor and proxy settings travel encrypted.
Disconnect VPN before applying received settings.
Scan this QR with the phone containing your settings, then confirm the import here.
Scan on the receiving device. For a TV without a camera, choose Receive on the TV and scan its QR with your phone.
The QR contains a pairing secret. Show it only to your own device. Received settings require confirmation before applying.
An encrypted splate-settings.v1.json file is stored in an existing WebDAV folder. Upload and download run when you choose.
The encryption password is not saved. Enter the same password on the other device. WebDAV credentials stay on this device and are excluded from the backup.
Includes proxy settings and sharing password
General settings will be applied to this device. Servers are added to existing entries by default.
This sends servers, subscriptions, Tor settings and the proxy password. Continue only for your own device that displayed this QR.
HTTP and SOCKS on one local port. Authentication is on by default; the client generates credentials and passes them to the VPN automatically. LAN sharing is independent.
Without authentication, other apps on this phone can access the local proxy.
Saved. An active VPN will reconnect.
New credentials saved. An active VPN will reconnect.
These credentials stay on this device and are excluded from cloud backups. Proxy authentication does not hide the VPN connection from your ISP.
Subscriptions, bridges, geodata, filters, cloud links and WebDAV. If the VPN is unavailable, downloads fail without switching to a direct connection.
Pings and checks over Wi-Fi only
These operations wait on mobile data. You can still use the current VPN; a skipped check does not mark a server as dead.
